name: agentic-code-plugin
description: Coordinates a main agent and parallel sub-agents, tuned for small local models.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Agents read and write project files and run checks, so the workspace must be trusted.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Agents need a real folder on disk to sandbox.

commands.title: Agentic: Choose checks for this folder

agentic.model.baseUrl.markdownDescription: Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp). Read from your user settings (or Remote settings in WSL/SSH) only: a project's `.vscode/settings.json` cannot change where your code and API key are sent.

agentic.model.name.description: Model name as the server knows it.

agentic.model.apiKey.markdownDeprecationMessage: Use the **Agentic: Set API key** command instead. It keeps the key in VS Code's secret storage. A key found here is moved there and removed from this file.
agentic.model.apiKey.markdownDescription: Deprecated. Use the **Agentic: Set API key** command, which keeps the key in VS Code's secret storage. Local servers usually need no key.

agentic.model.contextWindow.description: Context window in tokens. Prompts are budgeted to fit inside it.

agentic.model.temperature.description: Sampling temperature. Low values make small models follow formats more reliably.

agentic.model.requestTimeoutMs.description: Stop a model request after the server has sent nothing for this many milliseconds. 0 (the default) never stops a request: you get a warning after agentic.model.silenceWarningMs and can press Stop yourself. The clock restarts whenever part of the reply arrives, so a reply that keeps streaming is never cut off. With agentic.model.stream off, nothing arrives until the reply is done.

agentic.model.silenceWarningMs.description: Warn when the model server has sent nothing for this many milliseconds (default 5 minutes). The request keeps waiting; the server may still be reading a long prompt, or may have dropped the request. 0 turns the warning off.

agentic.model.stream.description: Stream replies from the model server. Text then arrives while the model thinks, so a proxy in front of the server does not cut off a silent connection (a 504 "timed out" error). Turn off only for a server that cannot stream.

agentic.model.maxConcurrentRequests.description: Most model requests sent to the server at the same time, counting the coordinator and all sub-agents. Others wait their turn in the extension. Raise it only if your server runs several requests in parallel (for example vLLM, or Ollama with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL). Read from user settings only; a project cannot change it.

agentic.model.maxOutputTokens.description: Longest reply in tokens, thinking included, sent to the server as max_tokens. 0 means no limit. A limit stops one long thinking run from holding the server for minutes, but a reply cut short fails its format check and is asked again. Read from user settings only; a project cannot change it.

agentic.model.structuredOutput.description: How to ask the server for JSON. If the server rejects a mode (for example Ollama's "failed to load model vocabulary required for format"), the extension falls back to json_object and then none by itself. Replies are always checked against the schema and retried, so none still works.

agentic.checks.markdownDescription: Default checks that decide whether a task is done. Before the first run in a folder, the chat proposes these plus commands it finds in the project (package.json scripts, pytest, cargo, go, dotnet, gradle, make) for you to edit and approve; your choice is saved per folder. Sub-agents can also ask to run extra checks, which you approve one by one. Example: `[{"name": "test", "command": "npm test"}]`. Checks from a project's own `.vscode/settings.json` are only suggestions: they are shown for your approval, and **Run commands** never runs them without asking.

agentic.chat.coordinatorHistoryTokens.description: Most tokens of earlier conversation the coordinator gets with each message. The server reads the whole prompt before it answers, so a long conversation makes every coordinator reply slower and can trigger 504 timeouts. 0 means as much as fits in agentic.model.contextWindow. Read from user settings only, so a project cannot make more of your conversation go to the model.

agentic.maxParallelWorkers.description: How many workers run at once. A single local GPU usually serves one request at a time, so higher values mostly help with remote or batched servers.

agentic.worker.maxTurns.description: Tool calls a worker may make on one task before it is stopped.

agentic.worker.maxFixRounds.description: How many times a worker is sent failing check output to fix before the task fails.

agentic.chat.historySize.description: How many recent chat conversations are kept. At least 3 are always kept. Older ones are deleted; their runs stay in the Tasks view.

enumDescriptions: Sub-agents carry out plans as soon as they are made.
agentic.chat.defaultMode.description: Mode for new conversations when none was used before.

agentic.autoApprove.editFiles.description: Sub-agents' file changes are written to the project right away. When off, each change opens in VS Code (a new file as its own editor, an edit as a side-by-side diff) and is only written when you press Accept in the chat. Files outside the workspace, .git, secrets, .agentic and VS Code settings and tasks are never writable. Only your user settings count: a project cannot turn this on.

agentic.autoApprove.sensitiveFiles.description: Changes to package.json files, lockfiles, build files (Makefile, pyproject.toml, setup.py, build.gradle, ...), CI (.github), dev containers, git hooks and .vscode files are written right away too. When off, they always wait for your Accept. Only your user settings count: a project cannot turn this on.

agentic.autoApprove.commands.description: Commands run without asking: checks (tests, lint, and ones a sub-agent requests) and the commands sub-agents run in the Agentic Code terminal. When off, each command is shown first and nothing runs until you allow it. Commands start in the project folder, but they run as you: a command or the script it starts can read files elsewhere and use the network, so only turn this on for projects you trust. Only your user settings count: a project cannot turn this on.

agentic.delegation.maxTasks.description: Most sub-agent tasks one plan may have. The coordinator is told to prefer many small tasks. How many run at the same time is agentic.maxParallelWorkers.

agentic.delegation.maxResearchers.description: Most read-only sub-agents the coordinator may send in one research round. How many run at the same time is agentic.maxParallelWorkers.

enumDescriptions: No check-ins, progress looks, result reviews or verification. Sub-agents' own checks still run, and every change still waits for your review unless Edit files is on.
One look at a sub-agent that seems stuck, no result reviews, and verification with at most one fix-up round.
Up to two looks at a stuck sub-agent, a progress look every 8 steps, each result reviewed once (sent back at most once), and verification with up to two fix-up rounds.
Up to four looks at a stuck sub-agent, a progress look every 4 steps, results sent back up to twice, and verification with up to four fix-up rounds. The most model calls.
agentic.delegation.oversight.description: How closely the coordinator watches and checks its sub-agents. It watches every step without model calls, and when a sub-agent seems stuck it looks at it and lets it continue, sends a note, or stops it (only after a note; drafts are kept). It also looks at progress every few steps, reviews each result against the task before it counts (sending it back with feedback when something is missing), and verifies the whole request before calling it done: the approved checks run once more on a copy with all drafts together, the drafts are read against your request, and fix-up rounds go back for what is left. After research it checks the answer covers your question. Each look, review and verification is a model call, so higher levels cost more. A review that cannot happen never counts as passed: those drafts wait for you even with Edit files on. Replaces checkIns, progressEvery, reviewRounds, verify and verifyRounds. Only your user settings count: a project cannot raise this.

agentic.delegation.maxModelCallsPerRun.description: Most model calls one run may make: every step of its sub-agents plus the coordinator's check-ins, progress looks, result reviews and answers to sub-agents. When a run reaches it, its sub-agents are stopped as if you pressed Stop, and their drafts are kept for your review (never written automatically). 0 means no limit. Only your user settings count: a project cannot raise this.

agentic.delegation.autoRetries.description: Times a sub-agent that failed (its checks kept failing, it ran out of steps, or a tool error stopped it) is started again on its own. The new attempt is told why the last one failed and sees what it had drafted. Not after you or the coordinator stopped it, and not once the run has used agentic.delegation.maxModelCallsPerRun, which every retry counts toward. 0 leaves every failure to you; you can still reopen or retry a sub-agent by hand. Read from user settings only, so a project cannot make more model calls happen.

agentic.delegation.maxResearchRounds.description: Research rounds one message may use. After a broad first round, the coordinator can send narrower researchers (for example one per file) when the reports are too general to answer from.

agentic.scratch.linkDirs.description: Dependency folders linked, not copied, into the scratch copy inside .agentic where checks run against pending changes, so they need no reinstall. Only node_modules, bower_components, .venv, venv, vendor, .tox, .gradle and target can be linked, and only from your user settings; a folder with secret files at its top level is not linked. Everything else is copied, without files that may hold secrets (.env, keys, credentials).

agentic.protectedFiles.markdownDescription: More files that may hold secrets, as globs relative to the project (for example `**/my-tokens.yml`). They are treated like the built-in list (`.env`, keys, `.npmrc`, cloud credentials and more): sub-agents cannot read, search or change them, and they are left out of the scratch copy. Patterns from your user settings and the project's settings are combined, so a project can add patterns but not remove yours.

scripts.e2e:replay: tsc -p tsconfig.e2e.json && AGENTIC_E2E_REPLAY=1 vitest run --config vitest.e2e.config.mts
scripts.check: npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test
